trust_decision.summary: Untrusted carrier text must never make Jaeger extraction throw: a malformed percent-encoding in the uber-trace-id header yields no span context (deserializeSpanContext returns null) and a malformed value in any uberctx-* header is skipped, both decided inside JaegerPropagator.extract/deserializeSpanContext while well-formed baggage is still applied.

landing_point.why: The advisory names a malformed uber-trace-id header; the only percent-decode of that header is decodeURIComponent(serializedString) inside deserializeSpanContext, reached from extract at line 98.

fix_sites.entry_point: JaegerPropagator.extract (public TextMapPropagator API; also constructed by the OTEL_PROPAGATORS and declarative-config factories in sdk-node)
fix_sites.module_kind: propagator implementation in a published npm package

fix_sites.entry_point: same entry point, baggage branch: JaegerPropagator.extract over uberctx-* carrier keys
fix_sites.module_kind: propagator implementation in a published npm package

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A malformed uber-trace-id must not discard valid uberctx-* baggage from the same carrier, one bad baggage entry must not drop its valid siblings, and well-formed percent-encoded values must still be decoded ('%25id%25' -> '%id%'). A single try/catch around extract() that returns the incoming context, or removing decodeURIComponent outright, breaks all three.

O6_input_shapes: trace-id header string whose whole value is a malformed escape ('%ZZ', '%')
trace-id header string with a malformed escape inside a percent-encoded composite ('abc%G:123:0:01')
well-formed percent-encoded trace-id header ('%3A' as the field separator) that must still decode
baggage value string with a malformed escape ('%ZZ') next to valid uberctx-* entries
carrier value delivered as an array; only element [0] is decoded (array handling predates the fix)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second baggage parser that percent-decodes without the try/catch guard
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The core W3C baggage parser already carries the identical try/catch, and the package holds two parsers side by side (parseKeyPairsIntoRecord and the newer streaming parseBaggageHeaderString at line 92); a maintainer writing another parser entry alongside them could easily omit the guard.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A third propagator factory route (auto-configuration-propagators or a baggage-prefix-aware wrapper) that reaches extract
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The propagator factory map is already duplicated verbatim at :329 and :432 (env route and declarative-config route), so a maintainer copying the pattern into a new configuration surface is plausible.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A decode on the round-trip/injection side (encode on inject, decode in a matching helper)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: inject already percent-encodes baggage values at line 73, so a 'keep decode symmetric with inject' helper is a natural place for a maintainer to add a second, unguarded decode.

O9_family: Unhandled exception / improper validation of untrusted header text (CWE-248, input-validation flavour) leading to denial of service

O10_build.toolchain: npm workspaces + nx/lerna monorepo, tsc project references (tsconfig.json/tsconfig.esm.json/tsconfig.esnext.json), mocha + nyc for tests
O10_build.project_tests: packages/opentelemetry-propagator-jaeger/test/JaegerPropagator.test.ts (mocha, package script: nyc mocha 'test/**/*.test.ts'); at the pinned commit it has no malformed-percent-encoding cases (grep for %ZZ/doesNotThrow/malformed returns nothing)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Wrap the body of extract() in one try/catch that returns the incoming context (or drop decodeURIComponent altogether), which silently loses valid baggage whenever only the trace header is malformed.

out_of_scope_notes: experimental/packages/opentelemetry-instrumentation-http/src/utils.ts:303 percent-decodes URL userinfo with no guard, but that is outgoing-request URL parsing, not header propagation; noted only, not pursued.

packages/opentelemetry-resources/src/detectors/EnvDetector.ts:106-114 and experimental/packages/configuration/src/FileConfigFactory.ts:155 also decode percent-encoded values, but from operator env/file config rather than propagated headers.

O1 was counted as 1 public entry point (JaegerPropagator.extract); the same class is also instantiated from two sdk-node factory maps (experimental/packages/opentelemetry-sdk-node/src/utils.ts:329 and :432) and via propagation.setGlobalPropagator, all reaching the same two sink sites, so no distinct second entry path exists.

single_site red flag: the fix touches two functions in one file (the baggage loop in extract and deserializeSpanContext), so strictly it is not 'one function at one place'; it is flagged because the whole fix stays in one file, one call graph, with no O2 site and no O8 route.
